note: Whether an input is a command the agent parses rather than prose, asserted by both sides. The daemon uses it to decide whether a shared-chat message keeps its `[sender]` attribution; the app uses it to decide whether to expect that message back in the transcript, because a command may produce no user turn to find. Each side used to own its own answer, and a command the app thought was prose produced a 'Send not confirmed yet' for a message that was delivered perfectly.
rule: Single line only. The first token decides: a slash followed by ONE segment of word characters, a bang followed by a word character, or a dollar followed by a space or word character. `#` is prose, because it is a markdown heading far more often than a command.
prose:
/clear
and here is a long unattributed paragraph
